issuing_body: Minnesota Attorney General, Medicaid Fraud Control Unit
title: Medicaid fraud charges including Driving Miss Daisy non-emergency medical transportation case
supports: Charles Omato and LaTonia Jackson were charged in a Minnesota Medicaid fraud case involving Driving Miss Daisy, a non-emergency medical transportation company.
The Attorney General alleged more than $1.4 million in Medicaid fraud through transportation services not provided and claims involving travel times that could not have occurred as billed.
The case was part of the PITSTOP66 multi-agency investigation involving Minnesota MFCU, HHS-OIG and the Minnesota Commerce Fraud Bureau, with FBI and DHS assistance.
does_not_support: The charging release does not establish guilt or a final restitution amount.
Do not treat the PITSTOP66 investigation as a single conspiracy unless a charging instrument says so.
status_followup: A current DHS excluded-provider list shows Charles Omato with a Medicare/Medicaid exclusion effective 2025-12-17, but this source record does not infer the disposition of the criminal case from that exclusion.
